title: resolution/1.0 - the one artifact arXMCP produces

registry_sha256.$comment: THE ENTIRE CROSS-REPO FRESHNESS MECHANISM. One comparison, no clocks, no mtimes, no network. Editing the registry without re-running the resolver turns CI red, and there is no way to forget.

counts.$comment: One key per member of the `resolution` enum, and `tests/test_schemas.py` asserts that correspondence structurally -- an enum member with no counts key is a state the summary silently swallows.

resolution.$comment: `not_applicable` is the resolver declining to adjudicate, and it is kept apart from `not_run` because the remedies differ -- `not_run` is closed by running the resolver, `not_applicable` by fixing the corpus. It is the value ADR-0003 and ADR-0005 already name (`pass`/`fail`/`not_run`/`not_applicable`), and arXMCP's CLAUDE.md 4.10 rule 3 binds the same spelling across the seam. Its live case: `documents.arxiv_version` is '' for every row in every notebook, so a `current` verdict for an entry declaring `version: vN` would assert a vN pin confirmed by bytes of unknown version. A byte-equal match against an unversioned corpus is not weak evidence for that pin -- it is no evidence for it.

matched_by.$comment: Ordered strongest to weakest. `quote_sha256` is byte-equality after normalization. `quote_containment` -- the chunk body CONTAINS the normalized quote -- is what actually survives a re-chunk that merges or splits the statement's chunk, and it reads `current`: containment is an identity claim, not a similarity score, which is why it sits above `fuzzy` and not beside it. `fuzzy` may never read `current`; similarity is not identity.

resolved_source_version.$comment: The source version this result was resolved against -- the arXiv vN, or null. Null is currently the ONLY honest value: the corpus records arxiv_version as '' for every row in every notebook (8/8 sampled in each), so nothing can fill this until the ingest backfill lands. It is present and nullable rather than absent so that a resolution which CAN say which version it read has somewhere to say it, and one that cannot is visibly silent rather than silently unversioned.

allOf.$comment: `current` REQUIRES a recomputed body digest. A resolver that says current without showing its work is rejected.

A FUZZY match can NEVER be current. Nearest-neighbour similarity is not identity - this is the single line that stops a dense-ANN retrieval system silently re-pointing a citation at a different theorem.
printed_number is a HINT. It is populated only on the ar5iv/LaTeXML path (36 of 66 chunks even on the flagship paper), and authors renumber between versions.

`not_applicable` must SAY why it declines, and it may never name a source version. The reason is what separates it from `not_run` for a reader: one means nobody ran the resolver, the other means the resolver ran and the corpus could not answer. And `resolved_source_version` is precisely the field whose absence forces this state -- a result that both declines on version grounds and names a version is incoherent.

`quote_containment` may read `current`, and that is the whole point of the rung: containment is an IDENTITY claim -- the statement is in the chunk or it is not -- where `fuzzy` is an estimate. It still owes the same evidence as any other current result (the first conditional above), and it must carry NO similarity score: a number there would invite exactly the reading that this is a near-miss. `not_applicable` is in the list because the version guard is orthogonal to the rung: an entry found by containment in a corpus that cannot name its arXiv version is withheld for the same reason one found by byte-equality is, and excluding it here would have forced the resolver to misreport the rung it actually used.
